prompt: Write a synchronized TaskQueue that never hands the same task to two workers, then finish WorkerPool so it starts at most 8 threads, drains the queue, and joins every thread before reporting the total.
explanation: Checking whether the queue is empty and removing the front task have to happen inside one synchronized method; if they were two separate calls, two workers could both pass the emptiness check and one would get a task that no longer exists. Each worker loops until take() returns null, which is how the pool knows the work is done without any sleeping. Joining every thread before reading the results is what makes the answer deterministic -- the totals are only complete once all the workers have stopped.
hints: Mark every TaskQueue method synchronized, so the empty check and the removal cannot be split apart by another thread.
A worker's loop is: Integer task = queue.take(); while (task != null) { record(task); task = queue.take(); }
Start all the threads in one loop and join them in a second loop -- starting and joining in the same loop would run the workers one after another.
